items.quote: DTA experiments were carried out with a Setaram SETSYS-18 DTA instrument (SETARAM, Caluire, France) allowing measurements up to 1750   C. Cylindrical samples of 3 mm in diameter and height were placed in alumina crucibles and heated and cooled at least twice with a rate of 5 K/min (and in particular cases additionally with 2 K/min) in an Ar atmosphere. Calibration measurements were performed using certified standards of pure Au, Ni, and Pd resulting in an accuracy of  1 K for the measured temperatures. The values for the enthalpy of melting, which were determined from the area below the melting peaks, have a much higher relative error which is tentatively estimated to be  20%.
items.stated_uncertainty: 1 K for the measured temperatures,  20% for the enthalpy of melting

items.quote: SEM was performed using the EPMA instrument described below in SEM mode.

EPMA measurements were carried out with a Jeol JXA-8100 instrument using pure Co and Al as standards. Phase compositions were analysed with a beam probing sample volumes of about 1 mm3 and averaging at least twelve measured points per phase. The relative error of the resulting compositions is 1%. The actual bulk compositions of the alloys were determined by averaging the EPMA results of 750e800 spot analyses per sample with spacings of 10 mm in three rectangular fields of about 100e300 mm in width and length. The EPMA values were finally calibrated by a comparison with values obtained by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES).

items.quote: For heat treatments, pieces of the alloy Ale40.7Co (all compositions given in at.% throughout this paper) were encapsulated in quartz ampoules which were evacuated and back-filled with argon several times before sealing them. After heat treatments for 3 weeks at 900   C or 1 week at 1100   C, the samples were quenched by breaking the ampoules in iced brine (10% NaCl solution).
